shortDescription: Syslog Policy configuration for Cisco Intersight

options.name: api_bearer_token
options.description: Bearer token for OAuth2 authentication with the Intersight API. When provided, I(api_key_id) and I(api_private_key) are not required and the C(cryptography) Python library is not needed. If not set, the value of the INTERSIGHT_API_BEARER_TOKEN environment variable is used.

options.name: api_key_id
options.description: Public API Key ID associated with the private key. If not set, the value of the INTERSIGHT_API_KEY_ID environment variable is used. Required if I(api_bearer_token) is not provided.

options.name: api_private_key
options.description: Filename (absolute path) or string of PEM formatted private key data to be used for Intersight API authentication. If a string is used, Ansible vault should be used to encrypt string data. Ex. ansible-vault encrypt_string --vault-id tme@/Users/dsoper/Documents/vault_password_file '-----BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY-----     <your private key data>     -----END EC PRIVATE KEY-----' If not set, the value of the INTERSIGHT_API_PRIVATE_KEY environment variable is used. Required if I(api_bearer_token) is not

options.name: api_uri
options.description: URI used to access the Intersight API. If not set, the value of the INTERSIGHT_API_URI environment variable is used.

options.name: description
options.description: The user-defined description for the Syslog Policy.

options.name: first_remote_logging_enabled
options.description: If C(true), enables the first remote syslog server destination.

options.name: first_remote_logging_hostname
options.description: Hostname or IP Address of the first syslog server where log should be stored. This parameter is required if C(first_remote_logging_enabled) is C(true).

options.name: first_remote_logging_minimum_severity
options.description: Lowest level of messages to be included in the first remote log.

options.name: first_remote_logging_port
options.description: Port number used for logging on first syslog server.

options.name: first_remote_logging_protocol
options.description: Transport layer protocol for transmission of log messages to first syslog server.

options.name: local_logging_minimum_severity
options.description: Lowest level of messages to be included in the local log.

options.name: name
options.description: The name assigned to the Syslog Policy.

options.name: organization
options.description: The name of the Organization this resource is assigned to.

options.name: second_remote_logging_enabled
options.description: If C(true), enables the second remote syslog server destination.

options.name: second_remote_logging_hostname
options.description: Hostname or IP Address of the second syslog server where log should be stored. This parameter is required if C(second_remote_logging_enabled) is C(true).

options.name: second_remote_logging_minimum_severity
options.description: Lowest level of messages to be included in the second remote log.

options.name: second_remote_logging_port
options.description: Port number used for logging on second syslog server.

options.name: second_remote_logging_protocol
options.description: Transport layer protocol for transmission of log messages to second syslog server.

options.name: state
options.description: If C(present), will verify the resource is present and will create if needed. If C(absent), will verify the resource is absent and will delete if needed.

options.name: tags
options.description: List of tags in Key:<user-defined key> Value:<user-defined value> format.

options.name: use_proxy
options.description: If C(no), it will not use a proxy, even if one is defined in an environment variable on the target hosts.

options.name: validate_certs
options.description: Boolean control for verifying the api_uri TLS certificate
